title: Applied LLMs: subject assistants, retrieval and adaptation
summary: 24 detailed lessons in applied LLM systems, from choosing a task to building grounded subject assistants. Study retrieval, evaluation, fine-tuning and tools through offline examples and explicitly prepared model workflows.

lessons.title: The subject assistant decision: prompts, retrieval or fine-tuning
lessons.outcome: A subject assistant is a system that helps someone perform a bounded task using a defined body of knowledge.
lessons.lab: Describe a request for the current conversion-rate definition requiring a citation.
lessons.verification: route retrieval; reason current cited evidence. contract has exact fields, an abstention policy and a family split.

lessons.title: Data-science task contracts and structured extraction
lessons.outcome: Structured extraction turns text into typed records, but valid JSON is only the first boundary.
lessons.lab: Validate visits 10, purchases 3 and assignment_unit account.
lessons.verification: conversion rate 0.3. invalid unit rejected; account remains explicit.

lessons.title: Prompt and context engineering with measurable boundaries
lessons.outcome: Prompt engineering defines a task and the information presented to a model.
lessons.lab: Build a prompt with one metric evidence item and a conversion-rate question.
lessons.verification: separate instruction, evidence and question fields, with template subject-v1. ValueError before context selection.

lessons.title: Corpus provenance, versions and evaluation isolation
lessons.outcome: A domain corpus is a versioned dataset.
lessons.lab: Add source=course-authored, permission=course-fixture and SHA256 to each local document.
lessons.verification: 6 complete records; all hashes contain64 characters. attack text remains data; restricted record remains restricted.

lessons.title: Chunking, overlap, offsets and context budgets
lessons.outcome: Chunking divides documents into retrieval units.
lessons.lab: Chunk one two three four five six seven with size 3 and overlap 1.
lessons.verification: chunks one two three, three four five and five six seven. empty list for empty text; one short chunk for the two-token source.

lessons.title: Lexical retrieval and BM25 from first principles
lessons.outcome: Lexical retrieval ranks documents using observed terms.
lessons.lab: Rank documents a=account randomization, b=visit counts and c=account outcomes for the query randomization.
lessons.verification: a ranks first with a positive score; the other scores are0. empty result for no documents; finite zero score for an empty document.

lessons.title: Embedding retrieval, similarity and representation limits
lessons.outcome: Embedding retrieval maps queries and documents to vectors and compares their geometry.
lessons.lab: Use query[1, 0, 0] and documents purchase[1, .1, 0], geometry[0, 1, 0], mixed[.5, .5, 0].
lessons.verification: purchase ranks first, mixed second, geometry last. top-ranked IDwrong is outside the authored relevant set.

lessons.title: Hybrid retrieval, reciprocal-rank fusion and reranking
lessons.outcome: Hybrid retrieval combines complementary candidate generators.
lessons.lab: Fuse lexical[a, b, c] and dense[b, d, a] with constant60.
lessons.verification: b ranks first, a second. ValueError for nonpositive constant; TypeError for non-string ID.

lessons.title: Metadata filtering and access-controlled retrieval
lessons.outcome: Access-controlled retrieval must prevent unauthorized material from entering candidate selection, answer context, caches and logs.
lessons.lab: Give a public-only request the six-document corpus and inspect admitted IDs.
lessons.verification: private-v1 absent before ranking. trace contains only public document IDs.

lessons.title: Query rewriting and bounded multi-hop retrieval
lessons.outcome: Query rewriting can translate a user's phrasing into terms that a retriever understands.
lessons.lab: Rewritebuy rate usingbuy->purchase while preserving the original question.
lessons.verification: rewrittenpurchase rate; original unchanged. restricted document never appears.

lessons.title: Grounded claims, citations and evidence-based abstention
lessons.outcome: Grounded answering requires a connection between each substantive claim and supporting evidence.
lessons.lab: Answer the conversion-definition question from the metric document and its first sentence.
lessons.verification: statusanswered; one claim; citation slices the exact sentence. rate.3 with input counts preserved.

lessons.title: Evaluating retrieval and answers with oracle controls
lessons.outcome: A RAG evaluation should identify where the pipeline failed.
lessons.lab: Use relevant IDs a, c and retrieved b, c, a.
lessons.verification: recall1; reciprocal rank.5. duplicate ID detected.

lessons.title: Paired reliability studies and family-aware uncertainty
lessons.outcome: Reliability comparisons require an explicit unit of independence.
lessons.lab: Use systemA errors q1=0, q2=0, q3=1 andB q1=1, q2=1, q3=0.
lessons.verification: differences[-1, -1, 1] by sortedID. test-based selection rejected.

lessons.title: Supervised fine-tuning data and answer-target masks
lessons.outcome: Supervised fine-tuning data specifies the behavior a model is asked to imitate.
lessons.lab: Use promptIDs[1, 2] andanswerIDs[5, 6, 3].
lessons.verification: inputs[1, 2, 5, 6]; labels[-100, 5, 6, 3]; 3 active targets. record excluded despite valid token arrays.

lessons.title: Full supervised fine-tuning of a tiny causal decoder
lessons.outcome: Full supervised fine-tuning updates all trainable model parameters on governed target examples.
lessons.lab: Use sequences[1, 2, 5, 3] and[1, 4, 6, 3], masking the first shifted target.
lessons.verification: inputs shape(2, 3); labels[[-100, 5, 3], [-100, 6, 3]]; 4 active targets. receipt says20 updates, 4 active training targets and no natural-language competence claim.

lessons.title: Low-rank adaptation: dimensions, gradients and a real update
lessons.outcome: Low-rank adaptation, or LoRA, freezes a base linear weight and learns an additive update represented by two smaller matrices.
lessons.lab: Construct W=I8, A=ones(8, 2)/8, B=zeros(2, 8), rank 2 and alpha 4, then count stored entries.
lessons.verification: 64 base entries, 32 trainable adapter entries and scale 2. The actual update has rank 1, within the configured bound 2; alpha 4 gives twice the alpha-2 delta.

lessons.title: Quantized frozen bases, adapter gradients and QLoRA limits
lessons.outcome: QLoRA combines a quantized frozen base with trainable low-rank adapters, allowing gradients to flow through computations involving the dequantized base into adapter parameters.
lessons.lab: QuantizeW[[.1, -.9], [1.7, -.2]] withscale1.7/7 andnearest-even rounding.
lessons.verification: codes[[0, -4], [7, -1]]. all four unimplemented claims explicitlyFalse.

lessons.title: Compare full and adapter fine-tuning on frozen tasks
lessons.outcome: A fair adaptation comparison starts both candidates from the same base state and uses the same training examples, target masks and held-out tasks.
lessons.lab: Create a seed 31 decoder and copy its state into full and adapted candidates.
lessons.verification: all initial base parameters equal. adapter96 entries; 20 updates each; scope literal-token task.

lessons.title: Preference optimization, DPO and the RLHF distinction
lessons.outcome: Preference optimization uses labels describing which of two responses is preferred.
lessons.lab: Set policy difference0, reference difference0, beta.5.
lessons.verification: losslog2. offline updateTrue; reward_model_trainedFalse; online_rlFalse.

lessons.title: Fine-tuning embeddings and a small reranker
lessons.outcome: Embedding and reranker fine-tuning adapts retrieval behavior rather than only answer generation.
lessons.lab: Use queries anddocuments equal to the2x2identity matrix, withpositive labels0, 1.
lessons.verification: score shape(2, 2); one positive perquery. actual gradient updatesTrue; pretrained_semantic_encoderFalse.

lessons.title: Optional pretrained-model adaptation with pinned offline artifacts
lessons.outcome: A realistic pretrained-model adaptation recipe introduces dependencies that the tiny offline exercises deliberately avoid: model weights, tokenizer files, chat templates, library versions, artifact licenses and larger resource needs.
lessons.lab: Read the supplied model manifest and identify model ID, revision and license note before any download.
lessons.verification: exact40-character revision and Apache-2.0 card note are present. pretrained executionunverified; no generated success receipt.

lessons.title: Structured tools for extraction, aggregation and data-science work
lessons.outcome: An LLM can help propose data-science operations, but the application should execute only typed, bounded operations whose semantics are understood.
lessons.lab: Use rowsA1, A3, B10 and the admittedgroup_mean request.
lessons.verification: A count 2 mean2; B count 1 mean10. descriptive statisticavailable; causal claimnot established.

lessons.title: Domain assistant boundaries: freshness, injection, budgets and traces
lessons.outcome: A production-oriented domain assistant needs controls around the model as well as a good prompt.
lessons.lab: Use fixedUTCnow2026-10-22 and a document published one day earlier under a two-day limit.
lessons.verification: freshTrue. answer admissionFalse; reasonstale evidence.

lessons.title: Capstone: a grounded and evaluated data-science subject assistant
lessons.outcome: A subject-assistant capstone should demonstrate an entire evidence path: task admission, authorized retrieval, versioned source selection, grounded output, deterministic data-science computation and independent evaluation.
lessons.lab: Ask the public assistant forconversion_definition.
lessons.verification: answered withmetric-v1 citation and source text. local_fixture_passTrue; production_gono-go.
